title: Security paper argues an AI’s words cannot be the final safety boundary
friendlyTitle: AI safety cannot depend only on what a model says it is thinking
summary: James Mickens argues that model explanations, chain-of-thought monitoring and language-based probes may not reliably describe the computation producing an action. The paper proposes stronger isolation, taint tracking and independent audits as a security floor beneath linguistic monitoring.
friendlySummary: A paper says an AI’s written explanation may not show how it really reached a decision. It recommends technical barriers that work even when the explanation is incomplete or misleading.
whyItMatters: As agents gain access to files, credentials and external systems, asking a model to explain or critique itself is not enough. Organisations need controls that constrain data flow and permissions regardless of what the model says it intends to do.
friendlyWhyItMatters: If an AI can use files or online tools, safety rules should limit what it can actually reach. A reassuring explanation is not the same as a secure system.
